This {{sc|Iesvs}} vvhich is {{sup|‖}} assumpted from you into heauen, shal so come as you haue seen him going into heauen.⊣ {{verse|chapter=1|verse=12}}† Then they returned to Hierusalem from the mount that is called Oliuet, which is by Hierusalem, distant a Sabboths iourney. {{verse|chapter=1|verse=13}}† And vvhen they vvere entred in, they vvent vp into an vpper chamber, vvhere abode {{MarginNote|margin=left|margin-width=65|text=∷ This visible companie was the true Churche of Christ, which he left & commaunded to keepe together til the comming of the Holy Ghost, by him to be further informed & furnished to gaine al natiōs to the same Societie.}}∷ Peter & Iohn, Iames and Andrevv, Philippe and Thomas, Bartholomevv and Mathevv, Iames of Alphæus and Simon Zelótes, and Iude of Iames. {{verse|chapter=1|verse=14}}† Al these vvere perseuering vvith one minde in praier vvith the {{MarginNote|margin=left|margin-width=65|text=∷ The Heretikes, some in the text, other in the margent, translate, ''Wiues'', to wit, of the Apostles, most impudently, knowing in their consciences that he meaneth the Maries & other holy women that folowed Christ. as ''Lu. 8, 2. 24, 10''. See Beza & the Engl. Bible 1579.}}∷ vvomen and {{sup|‖}} {{sc|Marie}} the mother of {{sc|Iesvs}}, and his brethren. {{verse|chapter=1|verse=15}}† {{MarginNote|margin=left|margin-width=65|text=The Epistle vpō S. Mathias day ''Febr. 24.''}}In those daies {{sup|‖}} Peter rising vp in the middes of the brethren, said: (and the multitude of persons together, vvas almost an hundred and tvventie) {{verse|chapter=1|verse=16}}† You men, brethren, the {{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=''Ps. 40, 9. Io. 13, 18.''}}* scripture must be fulfilled vvhich the holy Ghost spake before by the mouth of Dauid concerning Iudas, vvho vvas the {{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=''Luc. 22, 47. Io. 18, 3.''}}* captaine of them that apprehended {{sc|Iesvs}}: {{verse|chapter=1|verse=17}}† vvho vvas numbred among vs and obteined the lot of this ministerie. {{verse|chapter=1|verse=18}}† And he in deede hath possessed a {{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=''Mt. 27, 5. 7.''}}* field of the revvard of iniquitie, and being hanged he burst in the middes, and al his bovvels gushed out. {{verse|chapter=1|verse=19}}† And it vvas made notorious to al the inhabitants of Hierusalem: so that the same field vvas called in their tonge, ''Hacel-dema'', that is to say, the field of bloud. {{verse|chapter=1|verse=20}}† For it is vvritten in the booke of Psalmes. {{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=''Psa. 68, 26.''}}* ''Be their habitation made desert, and be there none to dvvel in it. '' {{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=''Ps. 108, 8.''}}* ''And his Bishoprike let an other take''. {{verse|chapter=1|verse=21}}† Therfore, of these men that haue assembled vvith vs, al the time that our Lord {{sc|Iesvs}} vvent in and vvent out among vs, {{verse|chapter=1|verse=22}}† beginning from the baptisme of Iohn vntil the day vvherein he vvas assumpted from vs, {{MarginNote|margin=left|margin-width=65|text=∷ No smal mysterie, that the number of the twelue Apostles must needes be made vp againe.}}∷ there must one of these be made a vvitnes vvith vs of his resurrection. {{verse|chapter=1|verse=23}}† And they appointed tvvo, Ioseph, vvho was called Bársabas, vvho vvas surnamed Iustus: and Mathias. {{verse|chapter=1|verse=24}}† And praying they said, Thou Lord that knovvest the harts of al men, shevv of these two, one, vvhom thou hast chosen, {{verse|chapter=1|verse=25}}† to take the place of this ministerie and Apostleship, from the vvhich Iudas hath preuaricated that he might goe to his ovvne place. {{verse|chapter=1|verse=26}}† And they gaue them {{sup|‖}} lottes, and the lot fel vpon Mathias, and he vvas numbered vvith the eleuen<noinclude>{{rh|||Apostles.⊣}}</noinclude>
